KEY MESSAGE 1...Today into tonight, a shortwave trough could 
spark another round of showers and storms, but it will be 
working against a relatively stable boundary layer.

A cold front currently situated across central portions of the 
region continues to sink southward, and should continue to make 
southwestward progress through this morning. This will leave our
region in the relatively cooler marine layer and more stable 
air mass north of the front. The net result is that our region 
should be in northeast to easterly flow, and cloudy conditions 
for much of the day. As a result, surface based instability is 
expected to be very limited, with mostly elevated instability 
present. 

Consequently, the risk for severe storms is still quite 
conditional and uncertain. Given how sharp of a mid level short 
wave trough is approaching, there will be ample forcing, but it 
is a question of if the elevated instability will be enough to 
sustain storms in our region.

With that said, some CAMs do feature scattered storms moving 
into parts of the area by late this afternoon and into tonight.
Confidence in details is relatively low, but should the region 
experience more destabilization and erosion of the marine layer
than is currently anticipated, storms will be capable of 
damaging winds, some hail, and perhaps an isolated tornado. The
greater risk of any severe storms will be toward our southern
and western zones. Locally heavy rainfall will also be a 
threat with any training showers and storms, even if a severe 
thunderstorm threat does not materialize. Portions of eastern PA
have been highlighted in a Slight Risk for excessive rainfall,
which could lead to localized flash flooding.

SPC maintains a Slight Risk (level 2 out of 5) for severe
thunderstorms for much of our area, but again, this risk is 
highly conditional and low confidence for today into tonight.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Hot and humid conditions are forecast across 
the region on Thursday. 

A strong marine layer influence today will keep highs mainly in
the 70s to low 80s in most areas. Following the brief cool down
in the marine layer today for most areas, hot and humid 
conditions are once again expected across the region on Thursday
as the frontal boundary lifts north again. With the front to 
the north, high temperatures are forecast to climb into the 
upper 80s to mid 90s for many areas (low to mid 80s far north).
These temperatures combined with dewpoints in the low to mid 
70s will again result in heat indices well into the 90s to low 
100s south of I-78, perhaps even as high as 105 degrees for 
Delmarva.

A new Heat Advisory was issued for portions of southeastern PA
and NJ. This advisory may need to be expanded into Delmarva if
the forecast for heat indices near 105 degrees holds. North of
the current advisory area, maximum heat indices are forecast to
top out in the low to mid 90s, thus the advisory is unlikely to
need to be expanded farther north.


KEY MESSAGE 3...Unsettled conditions will continue on Thursday 
with the potential for severe thunderstorms. Scattered 
thunderstorms are again possible on Friday, mainly south of 
Philadelphia.

Another round of severe thunderstorms are possible on Thursday.
Friday could also experience a few severe storms across 
Delmarva, depending on how quickly the frontal boundary pushes 
south.

SPC has a Slight Risk (level 2 out of 5) for severe 
thunderstorms on Thursday for Delmarva and a Marginal Risk 
(level 1) to as far north as the I-78 corridor. 

The northwest flow pattern will remain in place on Thursday and
will continue to be supportive of all severe threats, including
damaging winds, large hail, and a few tornadoes, depending on 
how all the mesoscale details pan out. The threat for flash 
flooding is typically lower with these patterns, but not zero. 
Training can still occur and a single locale could have multiple
days with heavy rainfall.

Friday's SPC outlook only includes general thunderstorms (no
severe risk), though there is still some uncertainty with this.
Our latest forecast has about a 30-40% chance of showers and 
thunderstorms near and south of Philadelphia.


KEY MESSAGE 4...The Labor Day Weekend will feature mostly dry 
weather with at or below normal temperatures and lower humidity.

By Saturday, current model consensus indicates the frontal 
boundary will be pushing well south of our region, with 
Canadian high pressure building across the Northeast and Mid-
Atlantic. This will largely end any shower and thunderstorm 
potential. Thus, Labor Day Weekend is still shaping up to 
feature nice weather, with temperatures trending at or slightly 
below normal and lower humidity. The only road bump at the 
moment, could be a cold front that approaches the forecast area 
very late on Monday.
